title: Normal Vitals by Age
body:
## Vitals by age band

| Age band | HR (bpm) | RR (/min) | SBP (mmHg) | Typical weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Neonate (birth–1 mo) | `100–180` | `30–60` | `60–90` | `3–5 kg` |
| Infant (1–12 mo) | `100–160` | `25–50` | `70–100` | `4–10 kg` |
| Toddler (1–3 y) | `90–150` | `20–30` | `80–110` | `10–14 kg` |
| Preschool (3–5 y) | `80–140` | `20–25` | `80–110` | `14–18 kg` |
| School-age (6–12 y) | `70–120` | `15–20` | `80–120` | `20–42 kg` |
| Adolescent (13–18 y) | `60–100` | `12–20` | `90–120` | `50–70 kg` |
| Adult | `60–100` | `12–20` | `90–140` | `70–80 kg` |

Note: ranges differ slightly between PALS, AHA and textbook tables. Use your protocol's card for documentation; use the band above for pattern recognition.

## Adult other normals

| Value | Normal |
|---|---|
| SpO2 room air | `94–99%` |
| Oral temp | `36.5–37.5 C` (`97.7–99.5 F`) |
| Rectal / core | about `0.5 C` higher than oral |
| Pulse pressure (SBP − DBP) | `30–40 mmHg` |
| Capillary refill | under `2 s` |
| Fasting glucose | `70–99 mg/dL` |
| Pain | `0–10` scale, patient-reported |

## Pediatric minimum SBP

This is the floor, not the normal. Below it, treat as hypotensive shock.

| Age | Minimum acceptable SBP |
|---|---|
| Term neonate (0–28 d) | `60 mmHg` |
| Infant 1–12 mo | `70 mmHg` |
| Child 1–10 y | `70 + (2 × age in years)` |
| Over 10 y | `90 mmHg` |

The 50th-percentile (expected) SBP for a child 1–10 y is `90 + (2 × age in years)`.

> **Trap:** Children hold blood pressure until they are nearly dead. Hypotension is a *late* sign. Tachycardia, cool mottled skin, delayed cap refill and a weak peripheral pulse come first.

## MAP

Mean arterial pressure is the average pressure pushing blood into organs.

- `MAP = (SBP + 2 × DBP) / 3`
- Equivalent: `MAP = DBP + (pulse pressure / 3)`
- Target floor `65 mmHg` for organ perfusion (sepsis, shock, post-ROSC). Some neuro protocols target `80–90`.
- Example: `110/70` gives `MAP = (110 + 140) / 3 = 83 mmHg`.

## Shock index

`Shock index = HR / SBP`

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0.5–0.7` | Normal |
| `0.8–0.9` | Watch closely |
| Over `0.9` | Occult shock likely |
| `1.0` or more | Significant shock, escalate |

Example: HR `120`, SBP `100` gives `1.2`. Both numbers are individually survivable-looking; together they are not.

## Orthostatic vitals

Measure supine after `2–3 min`, then repeat after standing `1–3 min` (sitting if the patient cannot stand).

Positive if any of:
- SBP drop of `20 mmHg` or more
- DBP drop of `10 mmHg` or more
- HR rise of `30 bpm` or more (`20 bpm` in adults over 65)
- Symptoms on standing (dizziness, near-syncope) even with unchanged numbers

> **On shift:** Stop the test the moment the patient feels faint. A positive orthostatic set plus a normal supine blood pressure still means volume depletion.
